newsitem.title: USA: Clinton proposes more screening for Medicare docs.
newsitem.headline: Clinton proposes more screening for Medicare docs.

text.p: President Clinton Tuesday proposed stiffer screening of health care providers who receive Medicare and Medicaid payments in order to fight fraud and abuse in the costly government health care programmes.

Clinton asked Congress to pass a bill called "The Medicare and Medicaid Fraud and Abuse Prevention Act," which would help bar unscrupulous doctors and medical firms from the government health care programmes for the elderly and poor.

Among other things, the legislation would let Medicare and Medicaid administrators deny anyone convicted of a felony the right to take part in the programmes and require participants to furnish their Social Security numbers so that applicants could be checked for past fraudulent activity.
"The best way to prevent fraud is to keep dishonest doctors and other scam artists out of the Medicare system in the first place," Clinton said at a White House ceremony.

Clinton's initiative reflected concern about the extent to which unlicensed doctors and others were bilking taxpayers. A recent General Accounting Office report estimated that fraud and abuse accounted for three to 10 percent of all Medicare spending, or $6 billion to $20 billion a year.

"Medicare and Medicaid are more than just programmes. They are the way we do honour to our parents...and care for our poorest and most vulnerable children. We cannot tolerate fraud that robs taxpayers even as it harms those whom we owe a great deal to," he said.

A White House fact sheet said the new legislation "follows on four years of focused effort by the Clinton administration that has helped save more than $20 billion in health care claims through policy changes, penalties, recoveries, claims denials and settlements," a White House fact sheet said.

However, Congress acted last year to create an information clearinghouse to try to reduce fraud in Medicare and Medicaid. The data bank was to have been established by Jan. 1, but the administration has not yet carried out the plan.
